encounters.cc: Routine follow-up visit for acromegaly management and assessment of IGF-1 suppression therapy.

lines: Routine follow-up visit for acromegaly management and assessment of IGF-1 suppression therapy.

The patient returns to the Endocrinology clinic for continued management of his acromegaly, now two years following his initial presentation with pituitary macroadenoma and subsequent initiation of medical therapy after declining surgical intervention.
He initially presented with progressive enlargement of his hands and feet, coarsening of facial features, and joint pain.
Laboratory evaluation at that time revealed markedly elevated insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels and a failure to suppress growth hormone (GH) following oral glucose administration.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed a pituitary macroadenoma.
The patient declined surgery and was started on octreotide, which led to partial improvement in symptoms and reduction in IGF-1 levels.
However, over the past 6 months, his IGF-1 levels have plateaued at an elevated range despite maximum tolerated doses of octreotide, and his soft tissue swelling has persisted.
- Recurrent duodenal ulcer disease (suspected Zollinger-Ellison syndrome)
- Father: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor and primary hyperparathyroidism

He has no headache, visual changes, or other systemic symptoms.

The decision is made to initiate an additional pharmacologic agent that acts through a different receptor to suppress GH secretion.
